Method of Attack: Information-stealing malware targeting YouTube content creators to steal authentication tokens and hijack channels
Runs anti-sandbox checks using open-source Chacal tool
Scrutinizes browser SQL database files to locate YouTube authentication tokens
Validates tokens by launching web browser in headless mode and adding stolen cookie
Collects YouTube channel information (channel name, subscriber count, creation date, monetization status, official artist channel status)
Uses Rod library for web automation and scraping to exfiltrate data stealthily
Attack Vector: Malware distributed via lures impersonating video editing software (OBS Studio, Adobe Premiere Pro, FL Studio, Ableton Live, Antares Auto-Tune Pro, Filmora)
Impersonation of game mods and cheats (Grand Theft Auto V, Counter-Strike Go, Call of Duty, Valorant, Roblox)
Cracks and token generators for Discord Nitro and Spotify Premium
Bundled with other info-stealers like RedLine and Vidar
Indicators of Compromise: Use of headless browser sessions controlled by Rod library
